# Ratte (01, engineer) — BAD-084

## Brief
`test/server/functions.test.mjs` and `test/server/account.test.mjs` each decide
whether a local Supabase stack is there with the same three lines:

```js
const reachable = await fn('validate', { method: 'OPTIONS' })
  .then(() => true).catch(() => false);
```

That asks only whether `fetch` resolved. It cannot tell a live stack from a
**half-up** one: the nine `supabase_*_bad-takes` containers running while
`supabase functions serve` is not. Kong is up on 54321 and answers the
preflight `503 {"message":"name resolution failed"}` — a perfectly resolved
fetch — so `reachable` is `true`, every test runs, and every test fails.

That state is live on this machine right now, so you can verify both branches
without starting or stopping anything. Observed: `podman ps` shows nine
containers Up 7 hours (healthy); `pgrep -fl 'supabase functions serve'` finds
nothing; `curl -X OPTIONS http://127.0.0.1:54321/functions/v1/validate` gives
503. A full `npm test` in that state reports 1770 tests, 114 failing, and all
114 are in these two files (111 + 3) — zero elsewhere. With the two files
excluded: 1649 tests, 0 failing.

What a LIVE stack answers is the other half of the discriminator, and it is
unambiguous: every function's `OPTIONS` goes through `preflight()` in
`server/supabase/functions/_shared/respond.mjs`, which returns
`new Response('ok', { headers: CORS })` — a 200 carrying
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Kong's 503 carries neither. Pick the
discriminator you can defend in the comment you leave, and say in that comment
why the weaker version was not enough.

Both files must end up agreeing. `account.test.mjs:17-20` says its conventions
are copied from `functions.test.mjs` on purpose rather than imported, because
that file is not a module other tests reach into; honour that — copy, do not
create a shared import — unless you can argue the other way in your Result.

The skip reason is half the deliverable. Today both files say only "local
Supabase not running — see server/README.md § Local development (podman:
DOCKER_HOST + -x edge-runtime,vector,logflare) …", which sends a reader of a
half-up stack to start a stack that is already running. A half-up stack needs
its own sentence naming the actual repair: the containers are up and
`supabase functions serve` is not. `server/README.md` § Local development has
the serve command; read it and point at the real fix.

Skipping is right here and does not make the suite vacuous: the authoritative
run is the `Server integration` CI check, and
`.github/workflows/server-ci.yml:241-272` fails the job if the suite reports
ANY skip at all. Do not weaken that; do not add a skip CI cannot see.

A design note worth your judgment, not a decision made for you: `dbRuntime` in
both files gates on `reachable &&`, so whatever you do to `reachable` changes
which of the two `dbtest` skip reasons a reader gets. Make sure the message a
half-up stack produces is the half-up one, not the container-runtime one.

## Ticket proposals
- **server-ci.yml's skip-reason grep never matches, so the skip gate prints no reasons** — suggested P2; created as [[BAD-085]] at P3 by Spud.
  Why: The Server integration guard fails the job on any skip and then prints 'Reasons:' followed by nothing. It greps 'skip: ' but node's test reporters never emit that string: the spec reporter renders a skip as '<glyph> name (0.1ms) # <reason>' and the tap reporter as 'ok 1 - name # SKIP <reason>'. The count is read correctly; only the diagnosis is silently empty. BAD-084 just made those reasons carry real information (half-up vs absent vs no-container-runtime, each naming a different repair), and the operator staring at a red CI job is exactly the reader they were written for. The step's own comment shows listing reasons was the intent: it records that grepping for ONE reason was the previous bug.
  Evidence: .github/workflows/server-ci.yml:270 runs: grep -oE "skip: .*" /tmp/server-tests.log. Observed 2026-09-16 in worktree bad-084-stack-probe: 'node --test --test-reporter=tap test/server/account.test.mjs | grep -oE "skip: .*"' prints nothing, while the same output contains 'ok 1 - a token whose seat has moved cannot delete the account # SKIP local Supabase is half-up - ...'. The default spec reporter renders the same reason after a bare '# '. A grep of '# SKIP .*' (tap) or the text after '# ' (spec) would match; the summary-count grep 'skipped [0-9]+' is unaffected and still works.

## Result
Both probes now discriminate on whether the OPTIONS preflight SUCCEEDS, not on whether fetch resolved. probeStack() is a byte-identical copy in test/server/functions.test.mjs (above itest) and test/server/account.test.mjs (above dbRuntime) — copied not imported, per the brief and account.test.mjs's header; verified identical with diff. Three outcomes: fetch rejects -> the old 'local Supabase not running' message, unchanged; any non-2xx -> a new half-up message naming the real repair ('the containers are up but the functions are not being served: run supabase functions serve --env-file supabase/.env.local from server/'); 2xx -> live. A 5xx is retried up to 3 times (200/400ms) because the cold-worker 502 documented in server-ci.yml's warmup step is the one transient 5xx and node --test probes validate from both files concurrently. dbtest's fallback is now stack.skip, so a half-up stack gets the half-up sentence, not the container-runtime one.

CORRECTION to the brief, which changed the design: Kong's 503 DOES carry Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (kong/2.8.1 stamps it on its own error response, on every route including a function that does not exist). A CORS-header check would therefore pass in exactly the state it is meant to catch; only the status discriminates. That fact and why the weaker checks fail are in the comment.

PROVEN on this machine against the live half-up stack (9 containers up 7h, no functions serve, OPTIONS -> 503), never starting or stopping anything. BEFORE: functions.test.mjs tests 118 / pass 7 / fail 111 / skipped 0, exit 1; account.test.mjs tests 3 / pass 0 / fail 3 / skipped 0, exit 1. AFTER: 121 / pass 0 / fail 0 / skipped 121, exit 0, every reason the half-up one. npm test on the final tree: tests 1770, pass 1648, fail 0, skipped 122, exit 0 (121 ours + 1 pre-existing 'mobile/node_modules is absent') — the 114 failures are gone and nothing else moved.

The LIVE branch I could not run for real (starting functions serve would destroy the fixture and take over the shared stack), so I exercised the discriminator directly with a stub on 54399 answering what preflight() answers: 200 'ok' + CORS -> functions.test.mjs ran 118 tests with skipped 0 and account.test.mjs 3 with skipped 0 (they then fail, correctly, against a stub that is not Supabase); 502-then-200 -> also live, skipped 0, proving the retry; always-503+ACAO -> 3 attempts then the half-up skip; SUPABASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1 -> one attempt, the unchanged 'not running' message. What I did NOT prove: a real supabase functions serve answering 200, and CI's run. Claim is that res.ok is the branch, not that a real stack was exercised.

Judgment recorded in the code: 7 SQL-only dbtest cases that genuinely passed against the half-up stack now skip, because dbRuntime stays gated on the stack. Kept deliberately — dbtest is a narrowing of itest, not its own lane; account.test.mjs's dbtests all call functions, so decoupling would break the two files' agreement and reintroduce red-on-half-up. Commented at the gate. Filed proposal 118 (P2): server-ci.yml's 'grep -oE "skip: .*"' never matches either node reporter, so the skip gate prints no reasons; the count grep is fine. No files touched outside the two deliverables; no commit.
